First, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/59041e6817cbf26f9de00de0ec864cea57f1a419877fe5c3203857c5488c7324.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y=-2x,$ and

- *leaves* though the outer curver $y=2x^2.$

Now, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y=2x^2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/0761073a5f7f417a07f35cb0b7c08dd0b4ea6bd84da71f3e474911ee036c546b.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[\,(3)-(2{x}^{2})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[3-2{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=-2x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/9ea5e5dd50dcd623532557e5365118ae5c9b950be059ba8c0069c7b36071f2c3.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[\,(3)-(-2x)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[3+2x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[3-2{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}{[3+2x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}({[3-2{x}^{2}]}^{2}-{[3+2x]}^{2})\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
